summary:
Dancing with the SARs is an interactive Earth-observation platform that transforms Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite observations into an engaging way to explore how our planet changes over time.

Using NASA-ISRO NISAR and ESA Sentinel-1 data, the platform brings satellite acquisition information, geographic footprints, and temporal observations together on an interactive 3D Earth. Users can explore satellite coverage, navigate historical and recent observations, compare changes across time, and investigate selected environmental and disaster-related case studies.

Unlike conventional satellite data portals, Dancing with the SARs emphasizes spatial exploration and visual storytelling, making complex radar observations easier to understand and explore.

Our goal is to make Earth-observation data more accessible and demonstrate how SAR technology can support disaster awareness, environmental monitoring, and a deeper understanding of our changing planet.
details:
What does Dancing with the SARs do?

Dancing with the SARs is an interactive geospatial platform designed to make Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations easier to explore and understand.

The application presents an interactive 3D Earth using CesiumJS, allowing users to explore satellite acquisition footprints and their geographic coverage. It integrates observation metadata from NASA-ISRO NISAR and ESA Sentinel-1, with temporal filtering to explore acquisitions across different dates.

How does it work?

The platform combines a web-based visualization frontend with a data-processing backend. Satellite acquisition metadata and geographic footprints are processed and presented on the globe. Users can interact with the map, explore observation coverage, navigate the timeline, and investigate selected case studies involving environmental changes and disasters.

Temporal comparison and difference-visualization features help users understand how radar observations can reveal changes that may not be apparent through conventional optical imagery.

Why is it important?

SAR technology can acquire observations during both daytime and nighttime and through cloud cover. This makes it valuable for monitoring floods, land deformation, vegetation, and other changes on Earth's surface.

By presenting these observations through an interactive and accessible interface, our project aims to bridge the gap between complex satellite datasets and people interested in understanding Earth's changing systems.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: React, Vite, JavaScript
  • 3D Geospatial Visualization: CesiumJS
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • Geospatial data processing and visualization
  • Web-based interactive timeline and spatial exploration

Innovation and Creativity

Our approach combines scientific data exploration, interactive 3D visualization, temporal analysis, and disaster-focused storytelling in one platform.

Rather than presenting satellite acquisitions as isolated records, Dancing with the SARs connects spatial coverage with time, allowing users to explore Earth's changing surface through a more intuitive experience.

The platform is designed to make advanced Earth-observation technology more approachable for students, researchers, educators, and the wider public.
